query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The application of high-pressure torsion at 200°C to induce severe plastic deformation in TiZrHfNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy will improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: TiZrHfNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy processed via spark plasma sintering at 1000°C under 50 MPa pressure
generation.intervention: Application of high-pressure torsion at 200°C for 5 revolutions
generation.conditions: Processed via spark plasma sintering at 1000°C under 50 MPa pressure, then subjected to high-pressure torsion at 200°C for 5 revolutions

generation.mechanism: Grain refinement and dislocation-induced plasticity leading to improved ductility and uniform deformability
generation.predicted_outcome: 30-40% increase in ductility and uniform deformability, with minimal loss in strength and impact-induced energy release
